name: Bond current yield
description: Computes a bond's current yield as its annual coupon payment divided by its current market price. It measures the income return relative to what the bond costs now.
notes: The result is a decimal, so multiply by 100 for a percentage. It reflects only coupon income and ignores any capital gain or loss at maturity, unlike yield to maturity.

name: Bond Price
description: Values a bond as the present value of its coupon stream plus the discounted face value, using the yield per period. It sums an annuity of coupons and the lump-sum redemption discounted over n periods.
notes: Coupon, yield, and periods must all be on the same per-period basis (e.g. semiannual). Price rises when yield falls and falls when yield rises; the result is the fair present value at that yield.

name: Approximate Yield to Maturity
description: Estimates a bond's annual yield to maturity by adding the coupon to the annualized capital gain or loss, then dividing by the average of face value and price. The result is expressed as a percentage.
notes: This is an approximation that avoids solving the exact YTM equation, so it drifts from the true yield for large discounts or premiums and long maturities. Coupon and n are on an annual basis.

name: Macaulay Duration (Level Coupon Bond)
description: Computes the Macaulay duration of a level-coupon bond, the weighted-average time to receive its cash flows, using a closed-form expression in the per-period yield, coupon rate, and number of periods. It measures the bond's effective maturity in periods.
notes: y and c are per-period rates as decimals, and n is the number of periods, so the answer is in periods, not years. The formula assumes a bond priced with level coupons.

name: Modified Duration (from Macaulay)
description: Converts Macaulay duration to modified duration by dividing by one plus the periodic yield, D/(1 + y/k). Modified duration approximates the percentage change in bond price for a one-unit change in yield.
notes: y is the annual yield as a decimal and k the number of coupon periods per year, so y/k is the per-period yield. The result estimates price sensitivity and shares D's time units.

name: Bond Convexity (Finite Difference)
description: Estimates bond convexity numerically from prices at a lower yield, a higher yield, and the current yield, (Pm + Pp - 2*P0)/(P0*dy^2). Convexity captures the curvature of the price-yield relationship that duration alone misses.
notes: Pm is the price if yield falls by dy and Pp if it rises by dy, using the same shift on both sides. dy is a decimal yield change; a larger dy reduces accuracy.

name: Effective Duration (Finite Difference)
description: Estimates effective duration numerically from bond prices after equal up and down yield shifts, (Pm - Pp)/(2*P0*dy). It measures the approximate percentage price change per unit change in yield, capturing embedded-option effects.
notes: Pm is the price if yield falls by dy and Pp if it rises by dy. dy is a decimal yield change; effective duration suits bonds with cash flows that change as yields move.

name: Yield to Maturity (Approximation Formula)
description: Approximates a bond's yield to maturity by combining the annual coupon with the amortized capital gain or loss over the average of face and current price, (C + (F - P)/n)/((F + P)/2). It gives a quick estimate without iterative solving.
notes: This is an approximation, not the exact IRR of the cash flows; it is least accurate for deep discounts or premiums. Enter C, F, and P in the same currency units.

name: Continuous Compounding Discount Factor
description: Computes the present-value discount factor exp(-r*t) under continuous compounding, giving how much one unit of currency received at time t is worth today at continuous rate r. Multiply a future amount by this factor to discount it to the present.
notes: The rate r is a continuous (force of interest) decimal, not an annual percentage compounded discretely; time t is in years matching r. The factor is always between 0 and 1 for positive r and t.

name: Effective Annual Rate (Continuous Compounding)
description: Converts a nominal continuously compounded rate r into the equivalent effective annual rate exp(r)-1, the actual proportional growth of money over one year. This lets a continuous rate be compared with rates quoted on an annual basis.
notes: The result is a decimal fraction, so 0.05127 means about 5.127%. The effective rate always exceeds the nominal continuous rate because of continuous compounding.

name: Fisher Equation (Exact Nominal Rate)
description: Combines a real rate r and an inflation rate i into the exact nominal rate (1+r)(1+i)-1. It gives the interest rate needed to achieve real return r once inflation i erodes purchasing power, rather than the simple approximation r+i.
notes: Both r and i are decimal fractions (0.03 = 3%). The exact form adds a cross term r*i that the approximation r+i omits, so it differs noticeably at high rates.

name: Real Rate of Return (Exact)
description: Computes the exact real rate of return (1+rn)/(1+inf)-1, adjusting a nominal return rn for inflation inf to give the true gain in purchasing power. It is the precise form of the Fisher relation, not the approximation rn-inf.
notes: Both rn and inf are decimal fractions. The exact formula gives a slightly smaller value than rn-inf; the difference grows as inflation rises.

name: Bond Price with Semiannual Coupons
description: Prices a bond paying m coupons a year from its annual coupon rate and yield (bond-equivalent convention).
notes: A 5 % 10-year bond yielding 6 % costs about 925.61 per 1000 face.

name: Yield to Maturity (Exact)
description: Solves the bond price equation for the annual yield to maturity that makes the discounted coupons and principal equal the price.
notes: Assumes coupons are reinvested at the same yield. The approximation formula is close only near par.

name: Yield to Call
description: Finds the yield assuming the bond is redeemed at the call price on the first call date.
notes: For premium callable bonds investors quote the lower of yield to call and yield to maturity (yield to worst).

name: Accrued Interest
description: Gives the interest the seller has earned since the last coupon date, which the buyer pays on top of the quoted (clean) price.
notes: Use 30/360 or actual/actual day counts as the market convention requires.

name: Dirty (Full) Bond Price
expression: clean + fv * c / m * d_since / d_period
description: Adds accrued interest to the quoted clean price to give the amount actually paid.
notes: Quotes use the clean price so it does not jump on coupon dates.

name: Bond Price from Spot Rates
expression: sum(k, 1, len(s), cpn / (1 + at(s, k))^k) + fv / (1 + at(s, len(s)))^len(s)
description: Prices a bond by discounting each cash flow at the spot (zero-coupon) rate for its own maturity — the arbitrage-free price.
notes: The last spot rate applies to the final coupon and the principal.

name: Par Yield from Spot Rates
description: Gives the coupon rate at which a bond with these spot rates would price at par. The same number is the fixed rate of a plain interest-rate swap.
notes: Par yield = (1 − d_n)/Σ d_k with discount factors d_k = (1 + s_k)^(−k).

name: Implied Forward Rate between Two Maturities
description: Gives the forward rate for borrowing from t₁ to t₂ locked in by today's spot rates.
notes: With 3 % for one year and 4 % for two, the 1-year rate one year ahead is about 5.01 %.

name: Continuous Forward Rate
description: Gives the forward rate between t₁ and t₂ with continuously compounded zero rates.
notes: Here 5 %: continuous rates combine linearly in time.

name: Macaulay Duration from a Cash-Flow List
expression: sum(k, 1, len(cf), k * at(cf, k) / (1 + y)^k) / sum(k, 1, len(cf), at(cf, k) / (1 + y)^k)
description: Computes the present-value-weighted average time to the cash flows of any bond or liability stream.
notes: Divide by the number of periods per year to express it in years.

name: Modified Duration from a Cash-Flow List
expression: sum(k, 1, len(cf), k * at(cf, k) / (1 + y)^k) / sum(k, 1, len(cf), at(cf, k) / (1 + y)^k) / (1 + y)
description: Gives the percentage price change per unit change in yield: Macaulay duration divided by (1 + y).
notes: A modified duration of 3.5 means a 1 % rise in yield lowers the price by about 3.5 %.

name: Convexity from a Cash-Flow List
expression: sum(k, 1, len(cf), k * (k + 1) * at(cf, k) / (1 + y)^(k + 2)) / sum(k, 1, len(cf), at(cf, k) / (1 + y)^k)
description: Computes the convexity (second derivative of price with respect to yield, over price) of a cash-flow stream.
notes: Positive convexity means prices rise more when yields fall than they fall when yields rise.

name: Bond Price Change: Duration and Convexity
description: Estimates the percentage price change for a yield change Δy with the second-order Taylor approximation −D·Δy + ½·C·Δy².
notes: A 1 % rise with duration 7.5 and convexity 70 gives about −7.15 %.

name: DV01 (Dollar Value of a Basis Point)
description: Gives the money change in value for a one-basis-point (0.01 %) change in yield.
notes: A 1,000,000 position with duration 7.5 moves about 750 per basis point.

name: Duration of a Perpetuity
description: Gives the Macaulay duration of a level perpetuity: (1 + y)/y.
notes: At 5 % a perpetual bond has a duration of 21 years, however long it lasts.

name: Portfolio Duration
description: Averages the durations of several bonds weighted by their market values.
notes: Used to match the duration of assets to liabilities (immunisation).

name: Treasury Bill Bank Discount Yield
description: Gives the discount yield quoted for US Treasury bills: discount over face, annualised on a 360-day year.
notes: Understates the true return, because it divides by face rather than price and uses 360 days.

name: Bond-Equivalent Yield of a T-Bill
description: Converts a Treasury bill's return to a 365-day simple yield on the price paid, for comparison with coupon bonds.
notes: Valid for bills of up to six months.

name: Money Market Yield (CD-Equivalent)
description: Gives the return on price on a 360-day basis, used to compare bills with certificates of deposit and other money-market instruments.
notes: Sits between the bank discount yield and the bond-equivalent yield.

name: Nelson–Siegel Yield Curve
expression: b0 + b1 * (1 - exp(-t / lam)) / (t / lam) + b2 * ((1 - exp(-t / lam)) / (t / lam) - exp(-t / lam))
description: Gives the zero rate at maturity t from the Nelson–Siegel model, used by many central banks to fit government yield curves.
notes: β₀ is the long-run level, β₀ + β₁ the short end, and β₂ adds a hump.

name: Svensson Yield Curve
description: Extends Nelson–Siegel with a second hump term (Svensson 1994); used by the ECB and the US Federal Reserve for published curves.
notes: The extra term lets the curve bend twice.

name: Default Probability from Credit Spread (Credit Triangle)
description: Estimates the annual default intensity implied by a credit spread: λ ≈ s/(1 − R).
notes: A 200 bp spread with 40 % recovery implies about a 3.3 % yearly default rate.

name: Survival Probability with Constant Hazard
description: Gives the chance that a borrower has not defaulted by time t under a constant default intensity λ.
notes: λ = 3.3 % gives about 84.8 % survival over five years.

name: Risky Zero-Coupon Bond Price
description: Prices a defaultable zero-coupon bond with recovery of market value: the risk-free rate is raised by the spread λ(1 − R).
notes: Duffie–Singleton reduced-form model.

name: Zero-Volatility Spread (Z-Spread)
expression: solve(z, -0.05, 0.5, sum(k, 1, len(cf), at(cf, k) / (1 + at(s, k) + z)^k) - price)

variables.label: Spot rates for the same periods

description: Finds the constant spread over the spot curve that reprices a bond's cash flows to its market price.
notes: Measures the extra yield investors demand for credit and liquidity risk.

name: Inflation-Indexed Principal
description: Scales the principal of an inflation-linked bond (TIPS, linkers) by the change in the price index.
notes: Coupons are paid on this adjusted principal.

name: Floating-Rate Note Coupon
description: Gives the next coupon of a floating-rate note: face times (reference rate + margin) for one period.
notes: Uses a simple fraction of a year; money-market conventions may use actual/360 day counts instead.

name: Forward Rate Agreement Settlement
description: Gives the amount paid at the start of the period on an FRA: the interest difference, discounted because it is paid up front.
notes: Positive means the buyer (who locked in borrowing at the contract rate) receives it.

name: Vasicek Zero-Coupon Bond Price
description: Prices a zero-coupon bond (face 1) in the Vasicek short-rate model dr = a(b − r)dt + σ dW.
notes: The formula is P = A·e^(−B r₀) with B = (1 − e^(−at))/a.

name: Cox–Ingersoll–Ross Zero-Coupon Bond Price
expression: (2 * sqrt(a^2 + 2 * sigma^2) * exp((a + sqrt(a^2 + 2 * sigma^2)) * t / 2) / ((a + sqrt(a^2 + 2 * sigma^2)) * (exp(sqrt(a^2 + 2 * sigma^2) * t) - 1) + 2 * sqrt(a^2 + 2 * sigma^2)))^(2 * a * b / sigma^2) * exp(-2 * (exp(sqrt(a^2 + 2 * sigma^2) * t) - 1) / ((a + sqrt(a^2 + 2 * sigma^2)) * (exp(sqrt(a^2 + 2 * sigma^2) * t) - 1) + 2 * sqrt(a^2 + 2 * sigma^2)) * r0)
description: Prices a zero-coupon bond (face 1) in the CIR model dr = a(b − r)dt + σ√r dW, where rates stay positive.
notes: Needs 2ab ≥ σ² (Feller condition) for the rate never to reach zero.

name: Bond Price with Continuous Compounding
expression: sum(k, 1, len(cf), at(cf, k) * exp(-y * at(tm, k)))
description: Prices a stream of cash flows at given times with a continuously compounded yield.
notes: The standard convention in derivatives textbooks (Hull).

name: Current Yield plus Pull-to-Par (Total Yield Estimate)
description: Adds the current yield and the yearly share of the move to par, a quick check on a bond's total return.
notes: Rougher than the yield to maturity, but easy to compute mentally.

name: Interest Rate Swap Value (Receive Fixed)

variables.label: Discount factors for the payment dates

description: Values a receive-fixed swap with annual payments: the fixed leg Σ K·dᵢ minus the floating leg 1 − dₙ, times notional.
notes: Zero when K equals the par swap rate.

name: Swap DV01

variables.label: Discount factors for the payment dates

description: Gives the change in value of a swap for a one-basis-point change in the fixed rate (the annuity times notional times 0.0001).
notes: Used to size hedges with swaps.

name: Zero Rate from a Discount Factor
description: Converts a discount factor into the annually compounded zero-coupon rate for its maturity.
notes: For continuous compounding use −ln(df)/t.

name: Continuous Rate from a Periodic Rate

variables.label: Rate compounded m times a year

description: Converts a rate compounded m times a year into the equivalent continuously compounded rate.
notes: 6 % semiannual is about 5.9118 % continuous.

name: Periodic Rate from a Continuous Rate
description: Converts a continuously compounded rate into the equivalent rate compounded m times a year.
notes: 5 % continuous is about 5.0314 % compounded quarterly.

name: 30/360 Day-Count Fraction
description: Gives the accrual fraction under the 30/360 convention used for many bonds and swaps (a simplified US rule: days 31 count as 30).
notes: Actual/360 and actual/365 simply divide the true number of days.

name: Money-Market Interest (Actual/360)
description: Gives simple interest for a deposit or loan quoted on an actual/360 basis, the convention for SOFR, €STR and most money markets.
notes: Sterling and some other markets use actual/365.
